title: The Find Rows and Columns and Decode algorithm for quantum expander codes
abstract: A new adaptation of the Find Erasures and Decode algorithm from classical to quantum expander codes is presented. It runs in linear time and is parallelizable to logarithmic depth. Compared to Small Set Flip and Small Set Find, the new algorithm avoids the overhead of considering the subsets of stabilizer generators, requires less expansion and corrects more errors.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, highly efficient quantum algorithm for decoding quantum expander codes. It significantly improves upon existing methods by achieving linear time complexity and logarithmic parallel depth. The development is crucial for advancing fault-tolerant quantum computation by enabling the correction of a larger fraction of errors in these quantum codes.
main_problem: The paper develops a faster and more efficient quantum adaptation of the 'Find Erasures and Decode' algorithm for quantum expander codes.
main_result: The new 'Find Rows and Columns and Decode' algorithm runs in linear time and is parallelizable to logarithmic depth, correcting significantly more errors than previous methods.
method: The method adapts classical decoding techniques by reformulating the decoding process using iterative subgraphs and peeling procedures derived from the graph structure of the expander code.
model_or_system: The work focuses on quantum CSS codes derived from lossless expander bipartite graphs, which are used to construct quantum expander codes for error correction.
key_observables: Error correction capability (number of correctable errors), time complexity (linear time, logarithmic depth), and the required expansion parameter $\delta$.
important_parameters: The lossless expansion parameter $\delta$, the maximum degree $d$, and the blocklength $\ell$.
main_assumptions: The analysis requires the lossless expansion parameter $\delta < 1/3$ for the presented algorithm to function optimally.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the quantum expander code structure, introducing the 'Find Rows and Columns and Decode' algorithm, detailing the steps involving row/column support computation and peeling, and concluding with a rigorous complexity analysis for both sequential and parallel execution.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly efficient theoretical tool for quantum error correction, which is fundamental to building fault-tolerant quantum computers, directly impacting the feasibility of large-scale quantum computation.
